source: Local time-class gate -- machine load, compiler and background processes move these numbers; NOT in CTest (AGENTS.md 4.4 rule 21: bench, not assertion). Run tools/check/check_perf_gates.ps1 to judge a build against this file.
note: The absolute lines come from SPEC.NF.PERF.02 (cat 10 MB >= 45 fps; full redraw <= 100 ms) and the relative line (max_regression_percent) is that requirement's own 'regression > 10% is FAIL'. Metric keys are exactly those the bench writes under "metrics" in its --json= output. direction names the better side. A gate with relative=false is judged only by its absolute line. capture.build_config belongs to the measurement contract: the gate FAILs on a sample from a different optimization level, because a Debug build inflates the write chain by 20-30x and its readings describe the compiler flags rather than the product.

capture.aggregation: median across runs -- the same rule the gate applies, so a reference and a reading are comparable
capture.build: msvc-bench preset (Ninja + MSVC, RelWithDebInfo), default config (dracula, Cascadia 14pt)
capture.supersedes: Two generations. (1) The first capture on this date ran the Debug default preset and reported cat 90.7 fps / scroll 7.15 ms / full redraw 12.5 ms / 0.68 MB/s. It did not record the optimization level, so numbers that looked like product cost were describing /Od /RTC1 code. (2) The first optimized capture (cat 736.828 fps / ingest 20.627 MB/s) predates G19, the framework-side single-width short-circuit inside aurora::unicode_cell_width; that primitive sits in the write chain, so the whole ladder moved together (chain 25.9 -> 41.1 MB/s). Superseded rather than rewritten in place: a benchmark reference has to say which build and which framework produced it.
capture.invocations: Three independent gate invocations of three bench processes each; each reference below is the median of that invocation's three medians

ungated.reason: Derivative of scroll_frame_ms_mean (1000 / mean); gating both would double-count one signal.
Count of measured frames, a sample-size diagnostic rather than a cost.
Derivative of cat_mb_per_s (bytes / wall); same signal counted twice.

Attribution rung: the producer chain alone (decode, parse, state machine, grid) with no session, no lock and no queue. Moving one rung usually moves its neighbours, so the product-facing rate is locked on cat_mb_per_s (B-7) instead. Only present with --write-side.

Attribution rung: the same corpus through Session (lock, dirty-row scan, damage queue) while the main thread drains the queue without painting; the gap to chain_mb_per_s is the session-side cost. Only present with --write-side.

gates.note: SPEC.NF.PERF.02's named metric: 10 MB fed through cat must hold >= 45 fps. Post-G19 capture: 749.806 / 755.213 / 773.022 across three invocations (3.1% span).

Three capture runs spanned 1.244-1.355 ms (8.8%): a 10% relative window would leave almost no room for background load, so only the requirement's absolute line judges it. A whole-screen paint regression also shows up in B-3 / B-5. Post-G19 the three invocations read 1.220 / 1.220 / 1.260 (3.3%), still not enough samples to reopen a relative line on a tail-free single metric.

One row dirty per frame: the cheapest view of the per-frame cost of dirty-row filtering, run splitting and colour resolution. Capture spread 1.2%; the post-G19 re-capture read 1.261 / 1.304 / 1.262 across three invocations (3.4% span, adverse side 3.3%).
Tail of B-3; capture spread 2.7%, so the tail is worth locking. Post-G19 re-capture 1.433 / 1.501 / 1.483 (4.7% span, adverse side 1.2%).
Frame cost while the 10 MB feed is in flight (whole-viewport dirty plus a concurrent producer thread). Capture spread 5.3%; post-G19 re-capture 1.324 / 1.334 / 1.294 (3.1% span, adverse side 0.8%).

Tail of B-5 with a wide capture spread (18.7% then, 9.4% on the post-G19 re-capture: 1.513-1.655) -- too wide for a 10% relative line. Judged instead against the requirement's own frame budget (1000 / 45 fps), so a periodic long frame that would drop under 45 fps reads red even while the mean looks healthy.

Ingestion throughput. The first capture left it out on the belief that a write-side defect pinned it (gating a defect would freeze it in as the contract); that belief was a Debug-build artifact -- the optimized rate is 20.6 MB/s, and after G19 landed in the framework the post-capture rate is 28.9 MB/s. Raw single runs are NOT stable (a five-run probe spanned 19.2-21.3, 10.3%), which is exactly why the gate judges the median of three: the three invocations behind this reference read 27.334 / 28.888 / 31.420, a 14.2% peak-to-peak span but only 5.4% on the adverse side (a higher-is-better metric can only fail downward), so the 10% relative line still has headroom. This number is not named by SPEC.NF.PERF.02: it catches write-side regressions that frame-time gates cannot see, since a slower producer simply yields fewer frames.
